science.title: Advanced optical imaging reveals hidden activity in blood immune cells
science.description: A routine blood sample contains a diverse collection of immune cells that can reveal important clues about health and disease. These cells, known as peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), are widely used to study infections, autoimmune disorders, cancer and the immune system's response to treatment. Scientists typically identify these cells using fluorescent labels that attach to specific surface markers. While effective, those methods provide limited information about how the cells are functioning and can alter the cells during preparation. As reported in Biophotonics Discovery, a recent study shows how advanced optical imaging can reveal a previously inaccessible layer of information: the metabolic activity of individual immune cells within a complex blood sample.

science.title: Quality gated multimodal fusion improves scene construction and interaction experience in augmented reality digital media
science.description: Augmented reality now carries a great deal of digital media production, yet its scene construction still suffers from registration drift, asynchronous sensor streams, unnatural interaction and excessive cognitive load. We address these coupled problems with an integrated framework. Hardware-triggered acquisition and timestamping disciplined by the Precision Time Protocol feed a quality-gated cross-modal attention model whose fusion weights follow per-modality reliability rather than fixed priors. A dynamic scene construction algorithm then couples semantic matching, layout optimization by covariance matrix adaptation and harmonic relighting, so that virtual content stays geometrically and photometrically consistent with the room around it, while an adaptive feedback policy driven by the decoder’s uncertainty estimates tunes interaction cues to the demand of the current task. On a corpus of 184 controlled sequences together with public benchmark subsets, running on a HoloLens 2 platform, the system reaches 91.4% fusion accuracy at a median end-to-end latency of 16.8 ms with a 95th percentile of 18.9 ms, and its robustness margin widens when two modalities degrade at once. A within-subjects user study (n = 50) recorded reliable gains in immersion, presence, usability, satisfaction and cognitive load, with an exploratory analysis suggesting that first-time users benefit more than experienced ones. The approach offers a coherent path toward AR digital media that remains usable beyond enthusiast audiences, although outdoor scalability, hardware dependence and long-session fatigue all remain open.

science.title: Effect of calcined lithium slag, copper tailings and tungsten tailings on the properties and microstructure of hybrid cements
science.description: The effects of desulfurized gypsum (DG) activation on the performance and hydration microstructure of composite materials were investigated, with calcined lithium slag (LS), copper tailings (CT), and tungsten tailings (TT) powders employed as supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs) to substitute 30 wt% of ordinary Portland cement (OPC), either individually or in binary blends. Hydration matrix of the hardened paste was evaluated using X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and mercury intrusion porosimetry (MIP). The purpose of this work was to reveal the activation paths of weak alkali synergy in combinations, and to establish quantitative criteria for experimental design. The calcined LS and CT supplied reactive SiO2 and Al2O3, whereas the calcined TT contributed a substantial quantity of amorphous SiO2. The calcination temperature of 850°C was selected to enhance the pozzolanic reactivity of LS, CT, and TT powders. The activation of DG also contributed to the potential strength of composites. The XRD and XPS results exhibited that the amorphous SiO2 and Al2O3 and the micro particle filling component were also necessary in the synergistic ratio of weak alkali activation. Compared with the samples doped with LS alone, the Si-O and the Si-Al bonds in the Aluminosilicate in the TT were weakened, the Si 2p binding energy measured by XPS decreased from 101.43 eV to 101.79 eV (Δ = − 0.36 eV) and 102.85 eV decreased to 102.44 eV (Δ = − 0.41 eV), respectively. The samples of combination solid wastes also conformed to such a composition ratio, which may contribute to form carboaluminations and ettringite. The XRD and TG test findings demonstrated that the mining solid waste had been activated, and their degree of hydration (DOH) were increasing accordingly. This work proposed a new idea of employing DG as a mild alkali to stimulate the activation of mining solid waste to produce cementitious materials.

science.title: Ligament-dependent joint gap behavior reveals limitations of gap-based tissue balancing in total knee arthroplasty
science.description: Soft tissue balancing is a key determinant of stability in total knee arthroplasty (TKA), yet the biomechanical interpretation of intraoperative gap assessment remains unclear. This study developed a subject-specific finite element model of a TKA knee to evaluate how collateral ligament release and tightening conditions influence joint gap behavior during simulated intraoperative laxity tests. The medial collateral ligament (MCL) and lateral collateral ligament (LCL) were modeled using nonlinear elastic elements, and ligament pretension was systematically varied under graded release and tightening conditions. Varus and valgus moments (5 Nm) were applied at 0°, 60°, and 90° flexion to quantify medial and lateral tibiofemoral gap changes. Comparison with in vivo fluoroscopic measurements from CAMS-Knee subject K5R showed comparable magnitudes of postoperative knee translation and previously reported biomechanical trends. Joint gap response was direction-specific, flexion-dependent, nonlinear, and partially coupled between compartments. At 90° flexion, extensive MCL release increased the medial gap by up to 85% under valgus loading, while extensive LCL release increased the lateral gap by up to 75–80% under varus loading. In contrast, sensitivity remained minimal (< 10%) in full extension. Ligament release produced disproportionately larger gap changes than equivalent tightening conditions. The findings indicate that joint gap measurements do not provide uniform or unique information about ligament behavior and are most informative in mid to deep flexion. Overall, the results highlight inherent limitations of gap-based tissue balancing and support a more structured, flexion-dependent interpretation of intraoperative gap assessment in TKA.
